question.leadin: Give the following about the Crusades.
question.text: The Fourth Crusade, in the early 1200s, ended with the crusaders deciding to sack this Christian city, the capital of the Byzantine Empire, because they had lost their original source of funding.
question.clue: A large portion of this city was burned during the Nika riots.

swap.leadin: His campaigns against the Vandals and the Ostrogoths were much aided by his generals Narses and Belisarius.
swap.text: Identify this ruler who built the Hagia Sophia and recodified laws in Corpus Juris Civilis.
swap.answerHtml: Justinian I or Justinian the Great [prompt on partial answer]
swap.answer: Justinian I or Justinian the Great
swap.clue: Much of the history of this leader was recorded by Procopius , who traveled with his general Belisarius .

question.leadin: Fans of two chariot racing teams, the Blues and the Greens, rioted in support of two condemned murderers in this event.
question.text: Name this 532 CE riot, which burned nearly half of the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire.
question.clue: Participants in this event wanted to crown Hypatius, but were outmaneuvered by the eunuch Narses and slaughtered by Mundus.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the general Belisarius.
swap.text: Belisarius spearheaded the reconquest of Ostrogothic Italy under this Byzantine Emperor, who was denoted "the Great." He is best known for his namesake legal code, which revised and clarified centuries of previous Roman law.
swap.answerHtml: Justinian I [or Justinian the Great or Flavius Petrus Sabbatius Iustinianus Augustus]
swap.clue: With help from his eunuch Narses, this ruler suppressed the Green and Blue factions of chariot fans, ending the Nika Riots.

question.leadin: This Byzantine general's last victory came in 559 A.D. when he defeated a force of Huns and Slavs outside of Constantinople.
question.text: Name this general who conquered the Vandal kingdom in Africa at the Battle of Tricameron and who went on to fight and conquer most of the Ostrogothic kingdom of Italy.
question.clue: He was ordered to depose Pope Silverius in favor of Vigilius, an act for which he later repented, and he married Antonina, a court favorite who wielded a good deal of influence.

swap.leadin: This woman apocryphally declared that "purple is the noblest shroud" during the Nika Riots.
swap.text: Name this empress of the Byzantine Empire who met her husband Justinian through their shared support for the Blue faction of the demes.
swap.clue: A ruler with this name, who as a child acted in a portrayal of Leda and the Swan, was called the "most depraved" in the Anecdota.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Byzantine Empire.
question.text: This Byzantine emperor lost the Battle of the Gates of Trajan to Tsar Samuel. However, this ruler got his revenge at the Battle of Kleidion where he gained his most notorious nickname after blinding prisoners.
question.answerHtml: Basil II [accept Basil the Bulgar Slayer or Basil Porphyrogenitus; Prompt on “Basil”]
question.clue: John Geometres wrote of how the "arrows of the Moesians broke the spears of the Avzonians" in describing this ruler's loss at the Battle of the Gates of Trajan.

swap.text: This Byzantine emperor defeated the Sassanids at the 627 Battle of Nineveh. Unfortunately for this emperor's reputation, the resulting peace was ended when the Muslims conquered all of Mesopotamia and North Africa.
swap.clue: He occupied royal residence at Dastgerd, and supposedly returned with the true cross from a campaign in .

question.text: Michael VIII founded this dynasty, which expelled the Crusaders from Constantinople in 1261 and were the last to rule Byzantium before the Turkish conquest in 1453.
question.clue: The most famous member of this family temporarily ended the Great Schism with the Second Council of Lyon after reclaiming Constantinople from the Latin Empire. That man, Michael VIII, established this family as the final Byzantine dynasty.

swap.leadin: Fulk of Neuilly agitated for this event.
swap.text: Name this campaign whose disastrous result occurred after a meeting with Philip of Swabia, the taking of Zara at the behest of Enrico Dandolo, and an attempt to overthrow Alexius III.
swap.clue: In order to obtain the support of one city state, the participants of this event agreed to sack the city of Zara in Hungary.

question.leadin: Answer the following about innovations created by the Mongols.
question.text: After founding the Mongol Empire, Genghis Khan created one of these systems, known as the Yassa, in order to maintain order. One of these systems created by Hammurabi of Babylon was carved into a stone stele.
question.answerHtml: law codes [accept reasonable equivalents, such as legal systems; prompt on laws or codes]
question.clue: One work of this kind included sections like the Digest and the Institutes.

swap.leadin: His Corpus Juris Civilis codified Roman law, and his numerous building projects included the Hagia Sofia.
swap.text: Name this husband of Theodora, a Byzantine emperor whose rule was chronicled by Procopius.
swap.answerHtml: Justinian I the Great [or Flavius Petrus Sabbatius or Favius Anicius Justinianus Magnus]

question.leadin: The "Headless Council" at Hieria, so nicknamed because none of the five great patriarchs were there, was convened by Constantine V to support this policy.
question.text: Name this Byzantine policy which opposed the veneration of religious images.
question.clue: This practice was carried out by mobs during the Dissolution of the Monasteries and again by the Puritans.

swap.leadin: Description acceptable. To accomplish this action, the men involved hid certain kinds of eggs and larvae in their bamboo canes.
swap.text: Identify this sixth-century event that was perpetrated by two Nestorian monks returning from China to Constantinople.
swap.answerHtml: smuggling silk into the Byzantine empire [accept obvious equivalents]
swap.answer: smuggling silk into the Byzantine empire

question.leadin: Identify these military groups from Eastern European history that emerged from protective details.
question.text: Basil the Bulgar-Slayer's pervasive and somewhat accurate paranoia that the Byzantine army was filled with drunken, bribable scoundrels led him to form this personal guard. This force was composed of hulking, angry vikings and was maintained by Byzantine rulers well through the reign of Alexius Comnenus.
question.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

swap.text: This porphyrogenitus Emperor became a legendary figure in Greek folklore called the "Marble King," who was saved from death by an angel who hid him in a cave. In non-deluded-Greek-nationalist-fantasyland, this man was killed by troops under Mehmet II.
swap.clue: In one battle, this man was relieved by ships commanded by Francesco Lecanella, who landed despite attacks from Admiral Baltoghlu.

question.text: This twelfth-century Byzantine princess became one of the first known women historians by penning the Alexiad, which narrates the dynasty-establishing reign of her father Alexios I.
question.answerHtml: Anna Comnena [or Anna Komnene; or Anna Comnenos; prompt on just her first or last name]
question.clue: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.

swap.text: The Sicilian Vespers were orchestrated in part by this Byzantine Emperor, who retook Constantinople from the Latin Empire and founded a namesake dynasty that ruled until 1453.
swap.answerHtml: Michael VIII Palaiologos [accept either of the second two underlined portions along with the first one; prompt on “Michael”]
swap.clue: This figure's diplomatic acumen and willingness to bankrupt his treasury helped Pedro III of Aragon, overthrowing Charles of Anjou in the Sicilian Vespers.

question.text: The reign of this Byzantine dynasty began after John III Ducas Vatatzes and his successor Michael VIII ended the Halosis and brought Constantinople under the control of the Empire of Nicaea. Its rulers included Constantine XI.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the invasion of Byzantine Greece by Murad II.
swap.text: At that time, the entire Peloponnese was under the control of this Despotate, which had been established circa 1349 by Byzantine emperor John VI Cantacuzenus, and then taken over by the Palaeologus dynasty. It was ruled from a site near ancient Sparta.
swap.clue: Before becoming emperor, Constantine ruled this despotate that encompassed much of the Peloponnese peninsula whose capital was Mystras.
